message.content: The sculpture most frequently cited as the quintessential icon of the 19th‑century art world is **“The Thinker” by Auguste Rodin**.  Though the finished bronze was cast in the early 1900s, Rodin began modeling the figure in 1902, and the concept itself had been in development since the 1880s.  Its powerful, contemplative pose and the way it captures the human psyche made it an instant classic—and it remains one of the most recognizable images of modern sculpture worldwide.
